terrain.format: float32 little-endian, row-major from north (minZ) to south, X east
terrain.source: AWS Terrain Tiles terrarium z13 (public domain), SRTM-class surface model
processing: box-blur smoothing of the surface model
water polygons clamped to -1.6 m seabed
road/path/rail corridor flattening toward median street-level samples
foreshore clamp to <= 0.45 m within 12 m of the waterline
90 m blend to 0 along the Stage A and Harbour Bridge site seams
final smoothing, clamp to [-1.6, 90] m, 5 cm rounding
terrain.provenance: derived: DEM sampled on the district grid and flattened for playability

authoredLandmarksRequired.name: Anzac Bridge
authoredLandmarksRequired.reason: Cable-stayed spans, pylons and cables are authored approximations over the real OSM deck ways.

limitations: Phase 6C relaxed-accuracy district: a stylised, playable recreation, not a survey.
Streets, footpaths, water, parks and building footprints are OSM-derived; rooflines, façades, heights without tags, terrain detail and infill sidewalks are labelled approximations.
Terrain is an SRTM-class surface model (roofs and canopy included) flattened along road corridors, under water, near the shore, and blended to 0 at the Stage A and bridge-site seams.
Water rings are hole-bridged simple polygons: islands are dry land inside the water mesh.
Bridge deck profiles above water are authored approximations (documented per bridge).
Tunnels are retained in data but not drawn; elevated viaducts over land are lifted generically.
No North Shore: the scope is clipped at the harbour channel and the Phase 5 bridge site.
Building styling is deterministic per footprint; no claim that a given façade matches the real building.
